name: Museum of Aviation
company: Museum of Aviation Foundation / US Air Force
customer: Aviation people, veterans, families, school groups
unique: More than eighty five aircraft and missiles across four buildings beside Robins Air Force Base, including an SR-71 Blackbird, a B-1B and a U-2, with restoration hangars you can watch through glass.
buzz: It is free and it is enormous, which nobody expects from a town this size. The restoration hangar and the Blackbird get the most photographs, and pilots who train here bring their families back.

name: Go Fish Education Center
unique: A fishing education center with native Georgia fish in tanks from tiny darters to alligator gar, a casting simulator, and a stocked pond outside where kids actually catch something.
buzz: Small enough to finish in an hour and good enough that people with no interest in fishing enjoy it. The gar tank stops everyone.

name: Georgia National Fair
unique: The state's official fair, eleven days of livestock shows, a draft horse pull, harness racing, concerts and a midway, held on a fairgrounds built for it rather than squeezed into a parking lot.
buzz: People plan vacations around it. The livestock barns and the horse shows are the part that makes it different from a carnival, and the food lines are a sport of their own.

name: Georgia National Fairgrounds and Agricenter
customer: Horse people, rodeo fans, trade show crowds
unique: A year round fairgrounds campus with arenas, barns and a covered equestrian complex that hosts rodeos, hunter jumper shows, tractor pulls and the state's biggest livestock events when the fair is not running.
buzz: Check the calendar before you go, because on a show weekend it is a working agricultural site and on an empty Tuesday it is a parking lot. The rodeos are the best free spending afternoon.

name: Little League Southeast Regional
unique: The Southeast regional tournament that sends one team to the Little League World Series, played at a purpose built park with six fields, and it is free to walk in and sit down.
buzz: Eleven and twelve year olds playing in front of a crowd with a World Series berth on the line. Locals take the week off to watch.

name: Georgia Skies Air Show at Robins AFB
company: US Air Force / Robins Air Force Base
unique: An open house and air show on an active Air Force base, free to the public, with static displays you can walk up to and a flying program that has drawn the Blue Angels.
buzz: Traffic is the price of admission. People arrive at dawn, park in the fields and spend the day, and the base opens areas you never otherwise see.

name: Perry Dogwood Festival
unique: A spring arts and crafts festival in the walkable blocks of historic downtown Perry, timed to the dogwoods and run by the city rather than a promoter.
buzz: The kind of festival that closes the streets and fills them. Good food, real vendors, and parking is still easy.

name: Historic Downtown Perry
customer: Walkers, diners, people escaping the interstate
unique: A grid of restored storefronts around Carroll Street with a bakery, a butcher, a bookshop and a fountain square, two minutes off I-75 and a world away from the exit ramp.
buzz: Locals use it as their evening. The restaurants are the draw and the square is where the town gathers.

name: Historic Depot Row and E.L. Greenway Welcome Center
unique: A row of historic railroad buildings on Armed Forces Boulevard including the 1940s depot and a small World War Two museum, telling how a farming crossroads became an air force town almost overnight.
buzz: Free, compact and better than the size suggests. The depot and the war exhibits fit together because the base is the reason the town exists.

name: Rigby's World
dates: Water park Memorial Day to Labor Day, complex year round
unique: A locally owned entertainment complex with a water park, go karts, bowling and an arcade in one place, which for a town this size is the whole summer.
buzz: The water park is the summer answer for every family in the county. It is not a national chain and the prices show it.

name: High Falls State Park
unique: A waterfall on the Towaliga River where the drop powered a mill town that is now gone, with the stone foundations still in the woods and a lake above the falls for paddling.
buzz: The falls after rain are the best short hike off I-75. Campers rate the sites above the water and the mill ruins are the part people photograph.

name: Lake Juliette
unique: A 3,600 acre power company reservoir with no jet skis allowed, clear water, standing timber and a striped bass fishery that locals keep quiet about.
buzz: Anglers describe it as the calmest big lake in middle Georgia. No wake, no crowds, and the stripers run deep in summer.

name: Forsythia Festival
customer: Families, antique hunters, craft fair people
unique: Forty years of closing the streets around the courthouse square for arts, crafts, food and music under the forsythia bushes the town is named after.
buzz: One of the older festivals in the region and still free. The antique shops on the square do their best weekend of the year.

name: Forsyth Historic District
unique: A courthouse square of 1890s storefronts and a residential grid of antebellum and Victorian houses, several of them open as shops, in a town Sherman's army passed through in 1864.
buzz: The square is intact and the houses are the reason people stop. Antique dealers have clustered here for decades.

name: Madison Historic District
company: City of Madison / Madison-Morgan Chamber of Commerce
customer: Architecture people, history travellers, day trippers from Atlanta
unique: One of the largest National Register historic districts in the state, a grid of antebellum, Greek Revival and Victorian houses that survived the Civil War, with a free self guided walking tour from the welcome center.
buzz: People call it the prettiest town in Georgia and mean it. The walking tour is free, the square has real restaurants, and three house museums are open for tours.

name: Madison-Morgan Cultural Center
customer: Art people, concert goers, architecture buffs
unique: An 1895 Romanesque Revival graded school saved and turned into a arts center, with the original classrooms intact, a fine art gallery and a 400 seat hall that programs music and theatre.
buzz: The building is the attraction and the programming is better than a town this size has any right to. The auditorium acoustics get mentioned in every review.

name: Hard Labor Creek State Park
unique: Almost six thousand acres of pine and hardwood with two lakes, twenty miles of trail, rental cabins and an eighteen hole golf course, an hour from Atlanta and rarely full.
buzz: The trails are the draw for hikers and the golf course is the local secret. Cabins book out for fall weekends.

name: Morgan County African American Museum
unique: A small museum in a historic Madison house on the Black families, churches, schools and businesses of Morgan County, filling in the half of the town's history the house tours leave out.
buzz: Visitors say it changed how they read the rest of Madison. Hours are limited and volunteers run it, so call first.

name: McDaniel-Tichenor House
unique: An 1887 house built for Governor Henry McDaniel and lived in by three generations of the same family, with the governor's papers and furniture still in the rooms.
buzz: Tours are by arrangement and the docents know the family history in detail. One of the best preserved Victorian interiors within an hour of Atlanta.

name: Downtown Monroe Historic District
unique: A courthouse square ringed by 1890s brick storefronts and a block of antique dealers, in a town that has quietly become the antiquing stop between Atlanta and Athens.
buzz: The antiques are the reason to come and the square is pleasant to walk. Saturdays are busy, weekdays you have it to yourself.

name: Vines Park and Mansion
unique: Twenty five acres of botanical gardens, ponds and specimen trees around a white columned mansion on Oak Grove Road, free to walk and mostly used by locals.
buzz: Wedding photographers have found it. For everyone else it is a free hour of garden that nobody driving past on Highway 78 knows is there.

name: Shaking Rock Park
unique: Granite outcrops scattered through the woods including one enormous boulder balanced so finely that a hand can rock it, on land that was once Governor George Gilmer's estate.
buzz: Everybody tries to move the rock and everybody fails. There is a beaver pond and a short trail, and the whole stop takes half an hour.

name: Oglethorpe County Courthouse
unique: A Romanesque Revival courthouse finished in 1887, the fourth on a site used for county business since a log courthouse went up in 1793.
buzz: The tower and the stonework make it the photograph of the town. Small square, working government, no ceremony.

name: Old Crawford Depot
unique: An 1848 granite depot built with quarried Georgia railroad cross ties, the last stone depot the Georgia Railroad put up, later used to store ammunition during the Civil War.
buzz: A granite building this old and this plain is rarer than it sounds. Rail historians make the trip for it and everybody else drives past.

name: Lexington Historic District
unique: A nineteenth century county seat where the historic district covers nearly the whole town, with a walking tour brochure available from any shop on Main Street and a Civil War era jail still standing.
buzz: Fifteen minutes from Athens and almost no one stops. The streets are quiet, the houses are original and the tour is free.

name: Bartram Trail in Oglethorpe County
unique: A marked section of the long distance trail that follows the route of naturalist William Bartram's 1770s travels, running through the county from Philomath toward Cherokee Corner.
buzz: Quiet woods, no crowds, and a story attached to every mile. The county prints maps and the local hiking club maintains the blazes.
